title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Irrigation servicing
audience: Irrigation servicing operators, including solo technicians, who sell seasonal checks and fault reporting at a price that reflects the work and the rules that apply.
learningOutcomes: Write an irrigation servicing offer with a clear promised result, a time frame, conditions and a return-visit guarantee
Identify the friction and risk an irrigation client carries and reduce them
Price a servicing offer on value and on cost, without relying on installation prices

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: 'I will check your sprinklers' is a service. 'I will test each zone against your schedule, record the run time and any fault, fix what is in scope, and send a written zone report within two working days' is an offer. The client buys a system that runs when it should, and a report they can act on. The two-day report time is example wording; set it from your own records.

instruction.heading: The five parts of an offer
instruction.body: A clear outcome (every zone tested, each fault listed, and the controller set to the local watering window); a time frame (the seasonal visit date); the work the client must do (controller and meter access, the water supply turned on, pets and vehicles clear of the valves); the certainty you provide (a zone report with photos, taken with consent); and the risk you carry (a return visit to recheck a repaired zone, within scope). Put the scope and exclusions in writing. Exclude repairs outside the agreed list, supply problems outside your control, and backflow testing, for which no source was found. Some plumbing work is regulated, so see the registration section below before you quote a repair. In Western Australia a quote becomes binding once accepted (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026). In Victoria a contract exists whether the agreement was verbal or written (Consumer Affairs Victoria, 9 July 2025).

instruction.heading: Reducing friction and the watering window
instruction.body: Record the access points, the controller location, the water meter and any valves the crew must not disturb, and send the visit window in one message. Plan test runs inside the watering window that applies. In Victoria, a watering system may run only between 6 pm and 10 am (Victorian Government, water.vic.gov.au, updated 13 January 2026). In NSW, Sydney Water allows drip and smart systems at any time, and sprinklers and irrigation before 10 am or after 4 pm (Sydney Water). The Hunter Water permanent rule in the Lower Hunter also allows irrigation before 10 am and after 4 pm (Bureau of Meteorology listing of Hunter Water, retrieved 8 November 2026). These sources do not confirm whether a test run counts as watering, so check with the water authority before testing outside the window.

instruction.heading: Guarantees and claims
instruction.body: Consumer guarantees for services apply and cannot be removed by contract. In Victoria, a tradesperson guarantees due care and skill, fitness for any specified purpose and completion within a reasonable time where none is set (Consumer Affairs Victoria, 9 July 2025). A business must be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (Consumer Victoria, 13 October 2023). Do not promise water savings or a percentage reduction unless you have measured it and can show the evidence. Check current ACCC guidance before publishing any measurable claim.

instruction.heading: Packages that step up in price
instruction.body: Good: a seasonal zone check and written report. Better: the check, plus a controller reschedule to the local watering window and a written schedule the client signs. Best: the Better tier, plus fault reporting between visits and a second check in the peak season. Council scopes use this language: the Central Coast Council (Tasmania) three-year schedule of rates includes irrigation maintenance and fault reporting (closing 10 November 2025), so fault reporting is a recognised scope line. No independent servicing price was found. Do not use installation prices as a servicing price. The Melbourne cost guide lists multi-zone automatic installation at $2,250, $3,600 and $5,400, and single-zone drip on a tap timer at $720 to $1,975 (What's the Damage, verified 1 November 2026). Those are installation figures. Price each tier from your own cost per productive hour, and show one total with GST status stated (WA Consumer Protection, 4 September 2026).

instruction.heading: Registration before you quote a repair
instruction.body: The Victorian Building Authority lists non-agricultural irrigation as a registered plumbing class. Applicants must show relevant competencies and recent experience in irrigation plumbing work, or Certificate II knowledge plus at least two years working under a licensed irrigation plumber (VBA, undated). The page does not say whether a servicing visit needs that registration, so confirm it before you quote any plumbing repair in Victoria. NSW licensing for irrigation is not confirmed in this lesson. Check the rule for each state you work in, and refer any repair outside your registration.

procedure: Write the outcome in one sentence, such as 'every zone runs on the schedule and each fault is listed in writing'.
Set a visit window inside the watering window that applies to the client's address.
List what the client must provide, such as controller and meter access, and reduce each step.
Add one certainty element: a zone report with photos, taken with consent.
Decide the return-visit guarantee and confirm you hold the registration for any repair in the offer.
Price from value, then check the rate against your own cost and time.

workedExamples.situation: A Melbourne client has a multi-zone system with front and back lawns and beds. The owner can offer a seasonal check, a check with a controller reschedule, or a check with fault reporting between visits. No independent servicing price is available to compare with.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Which tier should the owner offer, and how should the price be set without a servicing benchmark?
workedExamples.reasoning: The owner offers the Better tier, because the controller reschedule solves the client's scheduling problem inside the Victorian window, and the written schedule is evidence the client can keep. The price comes from the owner's own cost per productive hour plus the margin, with the test time as named lines, and not from the installation prices. Any repair found on the check is quoted separately, after the owner has confirmed that the repair is within scope and that the registration covers it.

equipmentAndPpe: Zone test log with run time, pressure observations and fault notes
Controller schedule record with the old and new settings

commonErrors.prevention: Build the servicing price from your own cost per productive hour, and keep installation figures separate.

commonErrors.error: Running test cycles outside the local watering window without checking the rule
commonErrors.prevention: Check the state and utility rule before a test run, and record the window used.

commonErrors.error: Quoting plumbing repairs without confirming the registration
commonErrors.prevention: Confirm the registration that applies before quoting any repair in Victoria, and refer work that is outside it.
List repairs outside the agreed list, supply problems and backflow testing as exclusions.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Business guidance only. This lesson does not grant any licence, registration or authority. Check state rules before acting.

Watering rules are set by state and utility. Victoria: watering systems may run only between 6 pm and 10 am. NSW (Sydney Water): drip and smart systems at any time; sprinklers and irrigation before 10 am or after 4 pm. NSW (Hunter Water, Lower Hunter): irrigation before 10 am and after 4 pm. Check the rule for the address before you promise a schedule.

Irrigation registration in Victoria is a plumbing registration class, and this lesson does not say whether servicing needs it. NSW irrigation licensing is not confirmed. Do not offer a regulated repair until the registration that applies in that state is confirmed.
No backflow testing rule was sourced for Victoria or NSW. Do not offer backflow testing until its rule is confirmed.

qualityStandard: Every servicing offer is written, states its exclusions, names the watering window used and says whether GST is included.
Each tier price is built from the operator's own costs, and no installation price is used as a servicing price.
documentationEvidence: Written offer with the outcome, schedule, exclusions and return-visit terms
Zone report with run times, faults and photos, taken with consent
Controller schedule record with the reason for each change
summary: A good servicing offer promises a checked system, a written report and a schedule that complies with the local rule.
Price servicing from your own costs, not from installation prices.
Confirm the registration that applies before you quote any repair.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of an irrigation servicing offer does the customer buy?
What should a return-visit guarantee on an irrigation check be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford
